verdicts.statement: The Great Depression after World War I was partly linked to the decision by most Western nations to return to the gold standard at the pre-war gold price.
verdicts.reason: The context states that the Depression was largely caused by most Western nations returning to the gold standard at the pre-war gold price after World War I.

verdicts.statement: The return to the gold standard at the pre-war gold price created deflationary monetary conditions.
verdicts.reason: The context explicitly says that monetary policy was thereby put into a deflationary setting.

verdicts.statement: Deflationary monetary conditions weakened many European economies over the following decade.
verdicts.reason: The context says the deflationary monetary setting would over the next decade slowly grind away at the health of many European economies.

verdicts.statement: By 1931, the reparations and war-debt system had collapsed.

verdicts.statement: By 1931, the United Kingdom had not fully recovered from World War I.
